newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro plans NOK 5 bln Norway-UK power link.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro plans NOK 5 bln Norway-UK power link.

text.p: Norsk Hydro ASA said on Tuesday it had started with state grid operator Statnett a technical and commercial study into a possible power cable across the North Sea to connect the electricity markets in Britain and Norway.

Total costs including land facilities in both countries were estimated at about five billion crowns, Norsk Hydro said. The Norway-Britain interconnector cable was expected to be in operation after 2000, it said.
The study for the electricity interconnector will be finalised in late 1997.
Statnett operates the transmission system for high voltage electricity in Norway, as well as cable connections with other countries.
Norsk Hydro has electricity production and trade, as well as industrial consumption in both Norway and Britain.
"Hydro wants to establish an interconnector to make long-term imports to Norway as well as short-term integration of the two markets possible," a statement from the companies said.
Statnett will be the owner/partowner of a future interconnector cable and the operator of the system.
The study will include a possible link from the interconnector to offshore petroleum installations in the North Sea.
